summary.text: A male neonate born at 36 weeks of gestation by C-section for placenta previa, weighing 2,970 g, had an uncomplicated delivery and routine nursery care. He passed urine and meconium within the first 24 hours and had regurgitations since birth. Persistent nonbilious emesis began on day 3 of life with mild abdominal distension, normal bowel sounds and no palpable mass.

Initial sepsis workup was conducted and electrolytes were normal. Intravenous antibiotics and hydration were initiated, and the neonate remained nil per os with a nasogastric tube on free drainage. Abdominal X-ray showed an abnormal gas pattern, an upper gastrointestinal series showed delayed gastric emptying with threadlike contrast passage, and ultrasonography showed features consistent with HPS, with pyloric muscle thickness 4.8 mm and canal length 17.2 mm.

Exploratory laparotomy on day 7 of age confirmed the diagnosis of HPS, and a pyloromyotomy was successfully completed. Feeding was well tolerated postoperatively and the baby was discharged two days after the surgery in stable condition. The authors report rapid resolution of vomiting, no postoperative complications, and follow-up showing appropriate weight gain and normal feeding tolerance.

ambiguities.issue: Electrolytes are reported normal during the initial workup, yet the Discussion later cites normalization of hydration and electrolyte levels after surgery.

normalization of hydration and electrolyte levels

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer that electrolytes were abnormal at presentation or that any electrolyte disturbance was present; the case discussion also says the case lacked electrolyte disturbances.

ambiguities.issue: The source says "the surgery" and "postoperatively" without naming whether this is the exploratory laparotomy, the pyloromyotomy or one operation comprising both; it also does not state that the pyloromyotomy was performed on day 7 or that the laparotomy preceded the pyloromyotomy.

the baby was discharged two days after the surgery

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign day 7 of age to the pyloromyotomy or a calendar day of discharge, and do not order postoperative feeding, discharge or follow-up against a specific one of the two procedures.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 2
Delayed gastric emptying and intermittent threadlike passage of the contrast at the antral levelThe blue arrow points to the large, contrast-filled structure in the left upper abdomen. This is indeed the distended stomach, which is the expected appearance in pyloric obstruction. The orange arrow points to a very thin, trickling column of contrast at the gastric outlet. This matches what is typically described as the “string sign,” representing contrast passing through a narrowed pyloric canal. The purple arrow points just distal to the pylorus, where almost no contrast is visible, consistent with paucity of contrast beyond the pylorus, a hallmark of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis
